subject: Temporary throughput safety net — pricing structure & short surge rebate request
messages:
From: Alice Morgan <alice@greenlinetech.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-07 08:12 -0700
Subject: Short-term surge protection + ask on rebate structure

Hi Jonas,

Quick one — we have a product launch on June 15 that will likely spike inference usage for ~10–14 days. Our current commit will cover baseline traffic but not the peak. Can Redwood provide a short-term throughput safety net (temporary quota increase or a soft headroom) and a one-time rebate if we hit the projected uplift? We need pricing and a simple PO/contract path today so procurement can sign off.

What I need from you:
- A firm price for a two-week provisional uplift (estimated +250% qps)
- What happens to billing if we exceed the uplift (overrun rates vs blended ramp)?
- Any precedent for a short-term rebate or true-up if we convert excess usage to committed volume after the launch

We’re on a tight timeline (PO by EOD tomorrow). I can loop in procurement if that helps.

Thanks — Alice
Alice Morgan
Head of Platform, Greenline Tech
---
Greenline Tech | alice@greenlinetech.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Alice Morgan <alice@greenlinetech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-07 10:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Short-term surge protection + ask on rebate structure

Alice — thanks for the heads up and congrats on the launch. We can support a provisional throughput uplift for the two-week window. High-level proposal below; I’ll attach a formal quote after you confirm numbers.

Proposal (provisional):
- Temporary uplift: +250% qps for 14 calendar days starting on 2027-06-15
- Rate for uplift window: blended price = hosted rate * 1.15 (instead of straight overrun rate), capped at an uplift ceiling of $0.045 per 1k tokens for generation requests.
- Overrun handling: if usage > provisional uplift during window, overrun billed at standard overrun tier (1.8x baseline list). We can cap overrun exposure to 20% of uplifted capacity for this event if Finance signs off.
- Conversion rebate: if Greenline converts the excess usage into a 12-month committed uplift within 30 days post-launch, Redwood will rebate 50% of the uplift window premium back as a credit applied over the first two invoices.

Next steps: confirm start date (we have buffer to pre-warm caches), and I’ll route a PO-ready quote and a short SOW to legal. Ben — can you confirm the overrun cap and whether Finance can accept the proposed 20% overrun cap? Karthik — help on whether we need to pin a model variant (quantized) for this uplift to preserve latency.

If procurement needs a PO template I can attach one.

Best,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Alice Morgan <alice@greenlinetech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-07 11:28 -0700
Subject: Re: Short-term surge protection + ask on rebate structure

Looping in Finance clarification. Alice — we can accept a 20% overrun exposure cap on top of the provisional uplift. Practical notes:
- If you hit more than (uplift + 20%) we’ll invoice the remainder at the overrun tier.
- To implement the cap we’ll need the PO to reference the temporary uplift plan and a maximum dollar cap (suggested: $35k for the two-week event based on your estimate).
- We’ll need a signed SOW or amendment referencing the rebate conversion term to apply the post-conversion credit.

Attaching: temporary_surge_quote_v2.xlsx (pricing breakout) and a simple PO template.

Ben Carter
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
[attachment: temporary_surge_quote_v2.xlsx]
From: Alice Morgan <alice@greenlinetech.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Greenline Tech Procurement <procurement@greenlinetech.com>
Date: 2027-06-07 15:42 -0700
Subject: Re: Short-term surge protection + ask on rebate structure

Thanks, Ben/Jonas — this looks workable. Procurement attached a PO (Greenline_PO_final.pdf) and wants two small clarifications before sign:
1) Can the rebate conversion window be 45 days instead of 30? Our internal approval cadence is tight right after launch.
2) Can the overrun cap reference a soft-cap first (notify at 90% of cap then bill only if exceeded)?

If you agree on (1) and (2) we’ll push the PO through today. We may also request a DocuSign path.

Alice
---
Procurement: procurement@greenlinetech.com
[attachment: Greenline_PO_final.pdf]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Alice Morgan <alice@greenlinetech.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-09 16:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Short-term surge protection + ask on rebate structure

Alice — quick confirmation from product/legal side:
- Rebate conversion window: we can extend to 45 days.
- Soft-cap notification: we will send automatic alerts at 90% of provisional uplift and again at 100%; billing only applies when 100%+ is reached. If you hit above the soft-cap we will not throttle during the launch.
- DocuSign: we’ll send the amendment via DocuSign once we receive your PO text inline referencing the temporary uplift (Ben — please confirm the exact amendment language we want in the PO).

Jonas — I’ll coordinate the pre-warm and flag any model variant advice. Ben — confirm the dollar cap we expect on the PO so Procurement can fill it in.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Product, Redwood Inference
